title: Starting a band with the Walker brothers and Phineas
summary: He began studying clarinet and organised a band with the Walker family and his friend Phineas, rehearsing to the delight of the neighbourhood and a bulldog.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: to put on my body and I am a brown-skinned man and I can't understand that but I used a cane about a couple of weeks and after that I forgot about the cane and that was it. Then I began to study the clarinet. I studied the clarinet and there were five buddies I had, they were called the Walker family. They too were from Georgia and Louisiana and -- Indian people and Negro people mixed.
Well, all of them they bought saxophones, the two brothers bought saxophones and one other bought a trumpet, so I got an idea, I'm going to create, I'm going to make a band.

13, 14, 15. I said I'm going to make this band and I was coming into high school too, so I studied the clarinet and the band what it seems those -- this boy's name, Phineas, Phineas was on the trumpet but he just wasn't playing that music and he was my best friend. I got that old cornet that I had and got -- looked at the chart and got down and started playing.

Now, we had -- in this band, we had -- at one point Albert Heights, a violinist, we had a pianist, beautiful pianist, he come from the southwest part of Washington, then we had a full band and by the way, we had a boy named Daniel Braseers(?) which later he became one of the greatest jazz trumpets that is known. They used to call him Georgetown, and he was in the band. So we were rehearsing and across the street, the man had

to eat a bulldog, he was bad, he wanted / everybody up, but when we were rehearsing, the bulldog, he'd walk in and get right under what's this boy's name, Phineas' feet and stay there. He must have loved what Phineas wasn't playing, because Phineas wasn't playing nothing. And Mama had to whisper, "that/ dumb dog," (unintelligible) Mama said, well, you stay there now and don't let nobody else come in. People coming in the windows and everything, so the dog took care of his business and then people baking cakes and all the people around us was happy about it and stuff lemondae and ham / so everybody come to rehearsal.
